patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH v3] mm: bypass swap readahead for zswap

version_history.subject: [PATCH v3] mm: bypass swap readahead for zswap

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch bypasses swap readahead for zswap, an in-memory synchronous backend similar to zram. The current implementation of swap readahead can lead to pointless prefetching of pages, causing increased anon residency and page cache thrashing. By bypassing readahead for zswap, the patch aims to reduce this overhead and improve performance. Measurements show significant gains in build time, zswap-in/out rates, and reduced swap readahead hits. The patch reuses existing code and adds a new helper function to check if a swap entry is synchronous.

review_comments.author: Barry Song
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer Barry Song questioned whether the performance gain from bypassing swap readahead for zswap is dependent on the page-cluster setting, suggesting testing with values 0 and 1 to confirm

Reviewer Barry Song expressed interest in knowing if similar performance gains would be observed when using specific configurations, and suggested adding a mention of the 'page-cluster' configuration to the changelog.

Gave Reviewed-by
review_comments.raw_body:
Hi Alexandre,

I assume your configuration is as below?

/ # cat /proc/sys/vm/page-cluster
3
/ # cat /sys/kernel/mm/swap/vma_ra_enabled
true

I am curious whether setting `/proc/sys/vm/page-cluster` to either 0
or 1 would result in the same performance gain on a zswap-enabled
system?

---

The change makes sense to me. I am just curious whether setting those
configurations would result in the same performance gain.

Maybe you can mention the `page-cluster` configuration in the changelog
as well.

review_comments.author: Yosry Ahmed
review_comments.summary: The reviewer notes a potential benefit of readahead for compressed swap, citing Kairui's LPC presentation, but acknowledges that this is not currently the case and assumes any future improvements would also apply to zswap.
review_comments.raw_body:
No objection here, I am just thinking about Kairui's LPC presentation
about how compressed swap can (in theory at least) still benefit from
readahead: https://lpc.events/event/20/contributions/2421/attachments/2116/4689/Better%20Anon%20(Swap)%20Readahead%20(2).pdf.

Seems like a big portion of the fault cost is still outside of
decompression and can benefit from readahead, but that isn't the case
today. I assume any future improvements to readahead and re-enabling
for zram would also cover zswap?

review_comments.author: Alexandre Ghiti
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer noted that the patch does not handle the case where zswap is disabled, and requested a check to be added to ensure that swap readahead is bypassed only when zswap is enabled.

Reviewer Alexandre Ghiti agreed to align zswap with zram, following Kairui's work, but no specific technical issue or suggestion was made.
sentiment_signals: patch needs additional handling for zswap disabled
review_comments.raw_body:
Hi Yosry,

On Wed, Oct 7, 2026 at 11:37 PM Yosry Ahmed <yosry@kernel.org> wrote:

Thanks,

Alex

review_comments.summary:
Reviewer noted that the patch does not handle the case where zswap is enabled but the tree is empty, which can lead to a static branch in disk-only systems.

Reviewer noted that the patch description's performance metrics are not sufficient to justify bypassing swap readahead for zswap, and requested more detailed analysis.

patches_submitted.subject: [PATCH 0/2] mm/zswap: batch the writeback IO

series_items.subject: [PATCH 1/2] mm/zswap: batch the writeback IO of consecutive entries
series_items.patch_summary: This patch optimizes zswap writeback by batching consecutive entries into a single IO operation, reducing the number of write requests and improving performance. The patch introduces a new struct to share state between all entries written back by one LRU walk, allowing for more efficient use of swap cache and iocost throttling. The changes were tested with kernel build results showing significant improvements in writeback efficiency and reduced IO pressure.

review_comments.author: Nhat Pham
review_comments.summary:
Reviewer Nhat Pham noted that the improvement in batching writeback IO is limited because physical swap allocation may not be contiguous by the time of writeback due to refaults and holes, which could be mitigated by using vswap.

Gave Acked-by
review_comments.raw_body:
The improvement is pretty big, but still only 1.3 :(

Is this because writeback entries are not contiguous in physical swap
space? Physical swap allocation algorithm has a bias for allocating
contiguous slots, but by writeback time we might have already punched
a bunch of holes (refaults etc.).

Ironically, vswap might help a bit here, because we defer physical
swap space allocation to right before writeback time... But who knows
:/

Anyway, I'll take the 20% :)

series_items.subject: [PATCH 2/2] mm/zswap: plug the writeback IO of an LRU walk
series_items.patch_summary: This patch series aims to improve the performance of zswap by plugging the writeback IO of an LRU walk, allowing the block layer to merge what the batch cannot. The author has provided benchmark results showing a significant reduction in write requests and iocost debt when the patch is applied.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: The patch series aims to improve the writeback IO performance of zswap by batching consecutive entries and plugging the LRU walk. This is achieved through two patches: the first batched writeback IO, while the second plugs the LRU walk to allow block layer merging.

review_comments.author: Christoph Hellwig
review_comments.summary: Provided a high-level perspective on the patch series, stating that it looks great from his point of view.
review_comments.raw_body:
On Wed, Oct 07, 2026 at 05:34:42PM +0200, Alexandre Ghiti wrote:
> Since commit 8f29aa226f82 ("mm/swap: introduce struct swap_io_ctx"),
> reclaim merges the swap writes of folios with consecutive slots into a
> single bio, but zswap writeback still issues one IO per entry. Patch 1
> makes each zswap LRU walk batch its writeback IO. Patch 2 plugs the
> walk, so that the block layer can merge what the batch cannot.

No a zswap expert, but from the high-level perspective this looks
great.

review_comments.author: Nhat Pham
review_comments.summary: Expressed enthusiasm for the patch series, noting a significant performance improvement. However, he questioned whether the writeback entries are contiguous in physical swap space.
review_comments.raw_body:

>
> So let the two functions that walk the zswap LRU, zswap_shrinker_scan()

> runs alone, and next to a sibling fio random writer with 10 times its

The improvement is pretty big, but still only 1.3 :(

Is this because writeback entries are not contiguous in physical swap

Ironically, vswap might help a bit here, because we defer physical

patches_acked.subject: Re: [PATCH v4 0/3] btrfs: fix a UAF where btrfs_root::dirty_list is freed but still referred
patches_acked.patch_summary: A patch series to fix a use-after-free (UAF) bug in btrfs where the dirty_list is freed but still referenced.

review_comments.author: Boris Burkov
review_comments.summary: Raised concern that the fix might not be sufficient and suggested a more conservative approach. Approved the fixes overall.

review_comments.author: Qu Wenruo
review_comments.summary: Removed the first patch from the series after reevaluating its necessity. Addressed Boris's concerns and acknowledged his review.
review_comments.raw_body:
在 2026/10/10 03:00, Boris Burkov 写道:
> On Fri, Oct 09, 2026 at 08:43:37AM +1030, Qu Wenruo wrote:
>> [CHANGELOG]
>> v4:
>> - Also cleanup qgroup swapped blocks and dirty_log_pages
>>    Which are only released during switch_commit_roots().
>>
>> v3:
>> - Use Yalagada's v2 fix as the final UAF fix
>>    The delayed list_del_init() call inside btrfs_put_root() is not
>>    safe as another racing ioctl can grab the quota root, extending
>>    its lifespan.

>> v2:
>> - Add extra patches to address Sashiko's comment

>> The first patch is to make lock consistent when accessing
>> btrfs_root::dirty_list, btrfs_fs_info::dirty_cowonly_roots and
>> btrfs_transaction::switch_commits.
>>
>> Normally it's not a big deal as the existing lock-holding callers are
>> also holding a trans handle, thus they can not race with transaction
>> committing.
>> But the last commit will change the cleanup timing, and Sashiko is not
>> happy with that, so make it more consistent and shut Sashiko up.

> the new callsite to actually do the removal outside a trans handle. Is

That part (the first patch) is a little overkilled.

The main reason that patch is introduced is to prepare for calling 
"list_del_init(&root->dirty_list);" during btrfs_put_root().

As we have some call sites that doesn't hold a trans handler.

But later I switched back to the v2 fix from Yalagada, which does the 
manual list_del_init() call instead of relying on btrfs_put_root().

>

> bugs, even if they are sort of unlikely. If I misunderstood and it's

I'll remove the first patch from the series.
